Subject: Collaborative sprint MAP — hypothesis-driven template and kickoff materials

Hi Sylvia / team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — as promised I put together a hypothesis-driven Mutual Action Plan (MAP) template that is tailored to a short evaluation sprint. The template is intentionally focused on:

- Business hypothesis and success criteria (what "good" looks like)
- Concrete acceptance tests (functional + non-functional)
- Owner assignments and escalation contacts
- 30/45-day milestone timeline with gating criteria
- Procurement and security checkpoints (placeholders you can fill)

I've attached the editable Google Doc (MAP_Hypothesis_Template_v0.1.gdoc) and a 2-slide summary you can forward to stakeholders (MAP_Sprint_1_Slides_v0.pptx). If helpful, we can convert the GDoc into a joint co-edit prior to kickoff.

Proposed next step: quick review by your technical lead + procurement contact and then a 30-day sprint kickoff the week of May 24. If procurement needs more runway we can switch to a 45-day timeline (template includes both).

Request: can you confirm the primary acceptance tests you want validated (latency SLA, payload size, data retention) and list the internal stakeholders who should be on the MAP? Once I have that I'll push a v0.2 with a security appendix and procurement steps.

Links / attachments:
- MAP template (attached)
- Slides (attached)
- Draft shared doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=MAP_Hypothesis_Template_v0.1

Thanks,

Hi Diego — thanks for sending. Quick notes from our side:

- This looks promising. Two immediate asks: can the MAP include a short security appendix that references SOC2 artifacts and our required data retention policy for PHI? We need to show that before any test data is uploaded.
- Procurement: please include a clear step for initial commercial terms + PO routing. Our procurement cycle might add 2–3 weeks unless we can align on a minimal pilot agreement.
- Acceptance tests: our primary concerns are (1) inference latency P95 under representative payloads, (2) end-to-end integration with our redaction pipeline, and (3) documented logs/audit for every request.

We are on a tight window — target decision by the end of June. If we can lock stakeholders and procurement contact quickly we should be good.

Can you copy your account rep and someone from legal/procurement on the next update?

Thanks,

Sylvia Ramos
Director of Engineering | Ava Diagnostics
sylvia@avadiag.com

Thanks Sylvia — good, practical asks. Short replies inline and next steps: 

- Security appendix: yes. I'll add a one-page security appendix to the MAP that references our SOC2 snapshot and a minimal data handling playbook for the sprint. That will be included in v0.2.
- Procurement step: adding a "commercial gating" line item (owner: Marissa) with an option for a limited pilot SOW or a PO-backed pilot to accelerate things. Marissa, can you confirm a lean template we can use if they want to proceed without a full SOW?
- Acceptance tests: Jonas — can you pick two representative payloads (small, large) and a P95 latency target we should commit to for the sprint? Also a short note on what metrics we'll capture for audit/logging.

Sylvia — based on your procurement note, I've also added an alternate 45-day timeline if the PO path adds time. If your procurement can do a PO quickly we stay at 30 days; otherwise we default to 45.

Attached: MAP_Hypothesis_Template_v0.2.gdoc (adds security appendix + procurement checklist). Please review and suggest edits directly in the doc.

If that all sounds OK let's tentatively schedule a 30-minute kickoff the week of May 24 to align stakeholders.

Cheers,
